pr_body:
Currently when restoring global state from the snapshot we create new metadata from existing one and then override it with fields from the snapshot. This behavior could keep custom metadata from the current state if it is not explicitly created in the snapshot.

This bug was discovered when trying to remove auto-followers by restoring from the snapshot created on an empty cluster. Surprisingly such restore did not removed anything while still deleting remotes and breaking auto-followers. 

Closes: #81247
Blocked by: #82019
pr_title: remove custom metadata if there is nothing to restore

review_comment: I might have missed it, but I did not find the test change that checks that we restore customs to empty?

Most of the functionality is covered by `org.elasticsearch.snapshots.CustomMetadataSnapshotIT#testRestoreCustomMetadata`, but you are right, the part of returning back to null settings is missing. I will add it.
Updated `CustomMetadataSnapshotIT` with `isSnapshottableMetadataInitialized` and added unit test for `removeCustomIf`

I created this default instead of `NonRestorableCustom`, but then noticed `context()`. I am checking if I should use `context().contains(XContentContext.SNAPSHOT) == false` as indication that custom should be excluded from the snapshot and restore. 

Currently this is not present for:
* org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.IndexGraveyard
* org.elasticsearch.license.LicensesMetadata
* org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.RepositoriesMetadata (already excluded)
* org.elasticsearch.cluster.coordination.ElasticsearchNodeCommand.UnknownMetadataCustom
* org.elasticsearch.xpack.core.watcher.WatcherMetadata
That list makes sense to me.
This part is tested in SystemDataStreamSnapshotIT and AutoscalingSnapshotsIT. I am working on creating a IT for the scenario mentioned in the pr description.
This behavior is also covered by CustomMetadataSnapshotIT
I think this is fine, though I would like to hear the opinion of @original-brownbear.

Provided the context values are all correct (this was a bit of an issue when me and Ievgen last checked if I remember correctly) this should be fine. I couldn't find any way this would not work since the context isn't something we read from the repo but just have per class => all good from my end.
